title: Aisle-level thermal simulation & provisioning — Colocation GPU pool
body:
Purpose:
Short planning sheet for aisle-level thermal simulation and capacity provisioning for initial on-prem/colocation GPU pools (private deployments + Dedicated POCs).

Scope:
- Target sites: SFO-01 colo (primary), IAD-02 colo (DR), on-prem lab (SJC) for validation racks
- Fleet mix (baseline): 40x H100-80GB (server-level TDP 700–750W), 8x A100-40GB (500W), 4x CPU-heavy inference boxes (250W)
- Initial deployment: 8 racks in SFO-01; 2 racks in IAD-02 as warm overflow

Key assumptions and derates:
- Nameplate power per H100 server: 2.8 kW (system + fans + overhead) — measured P95 from bench: 2.5 kW
- PDU usable per rack: 11kW (after breaker/cable derate); plan margin: 0.85 safety factor => effective budget 9.35 kW/rack
- Floor loading allowed: 3500 lbs/rack (colo spec), average estimated 2700 lbs/rack with liquid-cool add-ons
- Target inlet temperature: 24°C, allowing up to 27°C peak before throttling
- Cooling redundancy: CRAC N+1 in SFO-01, CRAC runtime headroom min 30% at 8-rack load

Thermal simulation notes (CFD runs):
- CFD engine: OpenFOAM-based pipeline, runs tagged v3.2-cfd-aisle.
- Inputs: rack heat maps (per-U), perforated tile layout, cold-aisle containment (full-height), raised-floor vent distribution 40/60 cold/hot split.
- Baseline run (no liquid cooling): peak cold-aisle inlet delta = +6.8°C at rack 4 (center of aisle), predicted hotspot at RU 10–12 on rear of rack 5.
- Passive mitigation: increase perforated tile open area from 60% -> 75% at tiles in front of top 12U; reduces delta to +3.2°C.
- Active mitigation (recommended): partial rear-door liquid cooling for racks 4–6 reduces per-rack heat rejected to CRAC by ~40%, spreading load and keeping CRAC headroom > 35%.

Per-rack power & capacity table (estimates):
- Rack 1–8: avg 2.6 kW/server * 8 servers = 20.8 kW/rack nameplate -> after 0.85 derate = 17.7 kW usable.
- BUT colo per-rack PDU limit: 11 kW -> -> therefore we must: 1) reduce server counts per rack to 5–6 H100 servers OR 2) use dual-rack PDUs + cross-rack feed (requires colo sign-off).

Proposed rack layout strategy (SFO-01):
- 8 racks arranged as two 4-rack cold aisles (containment) with hot aisle return plenum.
- Rack roles: R1-R2 (low-density control + network + storage), R3-R6 (GPU compute), R7-R8 (spares + staging + liquid-door equipment).
- Plan to limit H100 density to 6 servers/rack (slotting 2U servers) to stay within PDU limits while preserving future headroom. This gives ~15.6 kW/rack nameplate -> 11 kW PDU constraint still tight; require colo upgrade or split power to two PDUs on separate feeds.

Cooling options evaluated:
- Option A: Increase cold-aisle containment efficiency + perforated tile tuning (low-cost, low-change) — good for < 8 racks; risk: limited scale, still high CRAC load.
- Option B: Rear-door heat exchangers (RDHx) on 3 racks (hotspots) — medium cost, reduces CRAC load by ~35% for targeted racks.
- Option C: Direct liquid cooling (full rack) — higher capex, reduces heat to CRAC substantially, requires drain and containment in colo; longer lead time (8–12 weeks).

Network & electrical provisioning notes:
- 2 x 100GbE per compute rack (leaf aggregation). Plan for fiber MPO breakout to meet colo cross-connect schedule.
- Breaker sizing: typical colo breaker per rack is 30A/208V (=> ~6.2kW per phase); we need dual 30A feeds or a single 60A if colo supports.
- UPS: aim for N (no ups on colo PDUs) + site UPS for CRAC + common systems; confirm with colo whether PDUs are on UPS-backed distribution.

Utilization & capacity planning (12 month view):
- Month 0: 8 racks SFO-01, base GPU count 40 H100 -> expected utilization for Redwood internal evals: 30–40% (background training/inference mix).
- Month 3: expected utilization climb to 55% for customer ramps; trigger thresholds: when 7-day avg GPU utilization > 60% or CPU queue latency > 200ms for tail -> spin up 2 additional racks or enable remote overflow to IAD-02.
- Growth plan: add 4 racks per quarter for first 2 quarters, then reassess once CRAC load > 65% sustained.

Operational runbook excerpts (checklist):
- Pre-provisioning checklist (before colo install):
  - [ ] Confirm tile layout and containment footprint with colo (ticket: INF-1423)
  - [ ] Secure dual PDU feeds per rack or approvable power-split diagram
  - [ ] Cold-start CFD run with final tile/cabinet geometry
  - [ ] Schedule RDHx lead-time (if chosen) and procurement approvals
- Commissioning checklist (day-of install):
  - [ ] Measure inlet temps at RU 1, 12, 24 across each rack
  - [ ] Validate PDU metering and breaker mapping in colo portal
  - [ ] Test network cross-connect and 100GbE links
  - [ ] Run soak test 72h at 70% synthetic load (stress scripts in infra-provisioning repo)
- Escalation matrix: primary SRE: Miguel Santos, backup: Evan Li, colo AM: Heather G. (external)

Risks & unresolved questions:
- Colo PDU limits are likely the gating item. We need explicit written confirmation from SFO-01 on available feed per bay. 
- Backpressure on CRAC during summer peak (Jul–Sep) could force throttling; mitigation: temporary capacity shift to IAD-02 or accelerate RDHx purchase.
- Floor drain availability for RDHx and liquid-loop maintenance not confirmed for SFO-01.

Cost & timeline (rough):
- Baseline (no RDHx): colo power increment + racks + cables ~ $220k initial (space + cross-connect + racking + cabling) + $4k/month colo space/power (est)
- With RDHx on 3 racks: +$45k CAPEX, lead 6–10 weeks -> lowers monthly CRAC/headroom margin but increases colo plumbing requirements.
- Decision point: choose Option A for immediate POC (deploy within 4 weeks) and schedule RDHx procurement if utilization hits 50% sustained for 14 days.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Asha: open power confirmation with SFO-01 colo (due 2025-09-12) — Jira INF-1423
- Priya: request floor-drain/maintenance info and RDHx vendor quotes (due 2025-09-16)
- Miguel: run updated CFD with perforated tile tuning (v3.2-run2) and share annotated temp maps (due 2025-09-15)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider hybrid approach: split H100 servers across two adjacent racks and cross-feed PDUs, reduces single-rack overcommit but increases cabling complexity.
- Look into colo offering for liquid-cooled bay (some providers have pre-plumbed racks) — could offset RDHx CAPEX if available.

Appendix (quick stats):
- Estimated total continuous heat load (8 racks, limited density): ~110 kW (before derate) -> CRAC must handle ~110 kW unless RDHx installed.
- Simulation artifacts stored: confluence page (linked), SFO-01 CAD floor plan attached in INF-1423 ticket.

Status: draft — not yet signed off.
